WORKFORCE / DATA CENTER CONSTRUCTION

Crew rooms the county
can say yes to.

For data center contractors, developers and workforce lodging operators.

Private rooms with their own bath for data center construction crews. Set on ground screws near the site and moved when the build is done.

Start a conversationSee the units

THE PROBLEM

Big builds bring big crews to small towns.

A large data center build can bring more workers than the town beside it has homes. Builds run for years. Crews need a room near the site, and the county wants a housing plan it can approve before it says yes to the project.

A CAMP THE COUNTY CAN APPROVE

Housing that helps the project get its yes.

Looks
Finished metal siding, charcoal trim and real windows. It reads as housing, not stacked containers.
Footprint
Ground screws, no slab. When units leave, the screws come out with them.
Scale
Start with a pilot cluster and add rows in phases, instead of one giant camp up front.
Privacy
One worker per room with a private bath. Two-key units for denser rows.
Afterwards
Units move to your next campus, or stay for operating staff where approvals allow.

PHASED WITH THE BUILD

Rooms that grow and shrink with your headcount.

  • Phase 1

    Site work

    A pilot cluster for early crews and supervisors proves the site, the utilities and the layout.

  • Phase 2

    Structure

    Add rows as headcount climbs. Same units and panels, no new design.

  • Phase 3

    Fit-out

    Often the peak. Two-key units add density, with accessible units where needed.

  • Phase 4

    Hand-over

    Units move to the next campus, or stay for operating staff and visiting technicians.

Each phase is scoped and quoted per project.
